clue.text: Projection angle must be adjusted after film's first showing

indicators.note: after places the rearranged angle behind the letter taken from film
the word first asks for only the opening letter of film's
something adjusted is altered, so the letters of angle are rearranged

explanation.surface: A projectionist is told to change the angle once the film has started showing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' looks like cinema talk beside 'film', but it is the definition: a jutting rim.
explanation.definitionFit: A flange is a protruding rim or collar on a wheel or pipe, a kind of projection.

clue.text: The infantry occupy a secure initial position

parts.note: foot soldiers are known collectively as the foot
to hold a place is to occupy it

explanation.surface: Foot soldiers take and hold a safe position at the start of an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A foothold is a firm first footing from which progress can be made.

clue.text: Charges leading to adverse criticisms

explanation.surface: Accusations that bring on hostile comment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an assault (soldiers' charges) and harsh verbal censure are called attacks.

clue.text: Fresh opportunity for resting actors

parts.note: green means fresh or new, as with green shoots
room can mean scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: A new chance for actors who are between jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resting' is theatre slang for out of work, but here the actors are simply waiting offstage.
explanation.definitionFit: The green room is the backstage lounge where performers wait when not on stage.

clue.text: WIndies left in tense situation at end of the day

indicators.note: in puts the West Indies and left letters inside the word for a tense spot

parts.note: a tight corner is a tense situation
WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies, whose cricket team is the Windies

explanation.surface: The West Indies cricket team are left in a tight spot as play closes for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The Windies are the West Indies cricket side; the setter capitalises WI to hint at the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim light at dusk, when daytime is ending.

clue.text: Legal document with empty words put before the recorder, perhaps

indicators.note: put before places the empty words ahead of the legal document

parts.note: wind is idle talk, words with nothing in them
an instrument is a formal legal document such as a deed

explanation.surface: A court recorder hears a legal document padded out with hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder in Britain is also a part-time judge, so the legal surface hides the flute.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorder is a woodwind instrument played by blowing, an example of the class.

clue.text: Relaxed in chalet — upstairs!

indicators.note: in says the answer is sitting inside the words chalet and upstairs

explanation.surface: Someone unwinds up in the top floor of a chalet.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is to ease off or slacken, so relaxed is its past sense.

clue.text: Irish boy 'needs to travel south without delay

parts.note: to go is to travel
S is the compass abbreviation for south
soon means shortly, without delay

explanation.surface: An Irish lad has to head south right away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossoon is an Anglo-Irish word for a lad or young servant, from French garcon.

clue.text: Peg, Pawnee's first English sweetheart, is at home here

parts.note: a tee is the small peg a golf ball sits on

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of Pawnee's

parts.note: read as sweet-heart, the central letter of the word sweet

explanation.surface: A Pawnee woman named Peg, an English girl's sweetheart, lives in a wigwam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' splits as the heart of 'sweet', its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tepee is the conical tent used as a dwelling by Plains peoples such as the Pawnee.

clue.text: Strangely rigid play — with drunk author!

indicators.note: strangely says the letters are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: A stiff play performed with a drunk writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a second anagram signal but is part of the fodder: RIGIDPLAY plus DRUNK gives the fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling wrote The Jungle Book and Kim, a famous English writer.

clue.text: Changing immediately after the performance

parts.note: on can mean straight after, as in on arrival
a turn is a performer's act on a variety bill

explanation.surface: A set change happens straight after the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk on the turn is starting to go sour, that is, in the process of altering.

clue.text: State reform exposes discrimination

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters of state are reshaped

explanation.surface: Political reform reveals prejudice in a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discrimination' suggests prejudice, but it is the fine judgement of taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is the ability to judge finely between things, discernment.

clue.text: The average sort of horse in London

explanation.surface: An ordinary horse found in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: HACKNEY is an inner borough of London; a hackney is also a horse for ordinary riding, hence hackneyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hackney is an everyday riding horse for hire, and Hackney is an area of East London.

clue.text: Better road show appearing on the island

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so road and show follow the island letter

parts.note: M stands for motorway, the main kind of British road
to prove something is to show it

explanation.surface: A roadshow on an island brings improvements.
explanation.definitionFit: To better something is to make it superior, to enhance it.

clue.text: Means of securing' stock, for instance, in an orchestra

indicators.note: in puts the for-instance word inside the orchestra's initials

parts.note: the LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra
as can mean for instance, as in cities such as Paris

explanation.surface: A rope, for example, among orchestra equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is livestock, caught by a rope with a running noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat with a noose is thrown to catch cattle, a tool for catching livestock.

clue.text: Orlando is unusual, having only one love — for the girl he marries

indicators.note: unusual says the letters are arranged in an unexpected way
love is zero, the letter O, and keeping only one drops the second O

explanation.surface: Orlando is unusual in being faithful to just one woman, the one he weds.
explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, Orlando marries Rosalind. 'having only one love' strips one O from ORLANDO, and 'unusual' rearranges ORLAND plus IS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's As You Like It the heroine weds Orlando at the play's close.

clue.text: Conductors are often energetic people

explanation.surface: Orchestra conductors tend to be lively types.
explanation.definitionFit: Live wires carry electric current, and the phrase also means lively, energetic people.

clue.text: Improvement in this is under way

explanation.surface: Things getting better while work goes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress means betterment, and something in progress is under way.

clue.text: Quite a blow for the farm worker

explanation.surface: A harsh shock for the farmhand.
explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a wild swinging punch, and also someone who cuts and dries grass on a farm.

clue.text: Bill has lines opposed

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad
verse is lines of poetry

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill contains clauses others resist.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means hostile or contrary, working against.

clue.text: Shield it from the guest

indicators.note: it from the guest means the word it is taken away from a word for guest

parts.note: a visitor is a guest
taken as written

explanation.surface: Protect something from the guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A visor is a screen protecting the eyes or face.

clue.text: Cheated by film with unexpected end

parts.note: a skin is a thin film or layer, as on hot milk

indicators.note: unexpected says the letters of end turn out in another order

explanation.surface: Viewers were cheated by a film with a twist ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' is the anagram signal working on 'end'; 'film' is a thin layer, not a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: To be skinned is slang for being swindled or fleeced.

clue.text: Wallow in a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Floundering about in muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To welter is to roll or wallow, and a welter is a confused jumble.

clue.text: Obscure new novel getting record coverage

indicators.note: coverage says the record letters wrap round the rearranged novel

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: new means the letters of novel are made into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A newly published book is getting press coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for 'novel'; 'coverage' puts the record round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap up and so hide from view, to conceal.

clue.text: Subject of a story going round, for example

parts.note: a story is a fib, a lie

indicators.note: going round means the abbreviation is turned back to front

explanation.surface: The theme of a tale that goes round, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a vassal owing feudal service, a subject of a lord.

clue.text: Infantile behaviour of bird with fish

parts.note: a mew is a gull, a seabird
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Childish antics from a bird with a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Mewling recalls Shakespeare's 'mewling and puking' infant.
explanation.definitionFit: Mewling is the feeble crying of a baby, whimpering.

clue.text: Toss, say, in anguish

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: to toss is to throw

explanation.surface: Tossing about in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A throe is a spasm of pain, agony.

clue.text: Lack of apprehension in darkness

explanation.surface: Not being frightened while in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' suggests fear, but here it means understanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge or grasp, figuratively being in the dark.

clue.text: Rebel leaders, free at last, unite to rise again

indicators.note: leaders takes the opening letters of rebel
at last picks the final letter of free

parts.note: to merge is to join or unite

explanation.surface: Rebel chiefs, finally freed, join forces to stage another uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: To reemerge is to come back into view, to surface once more.

clue.text: A point about the team which players appear to miss

parts.note: a side is a team
S, south, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A point concerning a team that its players seem to overlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' are actors, not sportsmen: an aside is heard by the audience while the others on stage pretend not to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides are remarks spoken to the audience that other characters supposedly do not hear.
